look_here_first: Start with flower color. White rosinweed is the standout Silphium in this project because its ray florets are white, while the nearby Silphium comparisons have yellow heads. Then confirm the tough rough/scabrous foliage, often deeply divided, on dry limestone or calcareous prairie.

key_traits.label: Best field traits
key_traits.text: herbaceous perennial; white-rayed composite heads; tough rough/hispid foliage; leaves often deeply pinnately lobed or divided; dry limestone/calcareous prairie and open slopes

key_traits.label: Comparison training
key_traits.text: White rays are the fastest split from nearby Silphium. S. laciniatum can also have deeply divided leaves but has yellow heads; S. radula has broad rough sessile leaves and yellow heads; S. integrifolium has broad entire leaves and yellow heads.

lookalikes.differences: Use white rays first, then leaf dissection and texture. Do not treat introduced Hays plantings as native-range evidence.
